response.answer:
### 1. Exception Funding vs. Cap Gap
Under **Article VII, Section 6**, no cap exception can fund a \$12.9m first-year Salary for a veteran free agent coming from a different Prior Team:
* **Traded Player Exception (TPE) (Art. VII §6(j))**: Applies strictly to player contracts acquired by assignment (trades), not direct FA signings [1].
* **Bird / Early Bird / Non-Bird Exceptions (Art. VII §6(b))**: Restricted exclusively to re-signing a team's own Veteran Free Agent [2].
* **MLE / BAE / DPE / Minimum / Rookie / Existing / Reinstatement (Art. VII §6(a)-(i), (k))**: Maximum allowable limits under Non-Taxpayer MLE (§6(e)), Taxpayer MLE (§6(f)), Room MLE (§6(g)), BAE (§6(d)), DPE (§6(c)), and Minimum (§6(i)) are all well below \$12.9m [3-8]. Existing Contracts (§6(a)) and Rookie Scale (§6(h)) do not apply to new veteran signings [2, 8].

Consequently, the contract must be funded directly via **Cap Room** under **Article VII, Section 5(b)** [9].

### 2. Summer Contracts & Roster Charge Net Impact
Under **Article VII, Section 4(i)**, a Summer Contract cannot provide Compensation protection prior to the Regular Season [10]. Because this contract includes protection at signing, it cannot bypass cap space requirements [9, 10]. 
Under **Article VII, Section 4(f)**, signing a player replaces at most one incomplete-roster cap hold (\$898,310) [11]. Thus, the conservative pre-signing positive cap gap lower test is **\$12.9m - \$898,310 = \$12.001690m** [11]. The \$100k trade acquisition tolerance under **Art. VII §6(j)(2)** cannot be applied to direct signings [12].

### 3. Unlikely Bonuses & Exception Extinguishment
Under **Article VII, Section 5(d)(2)**, a \$1m Unlikely Bonus is excluded from Team Salary, but Room is deemed reduced by all Unlikely Bonuses signed in that Salary Cap Year [13]. 
Under **Article VII, Section 6(m)(1)-(2)**, using cap space to sign a free agent extinguishes pre-existing unused exceptions (MLE, BAE, pre-existing TPEs) [14, 15]. Removing a later TPE alternative requires a complete witness confirming no intervening transaction generated a new TPE [1, 15].

### 4. Premises & Counterexample
* **Minimum Evidence Premises**: Execution timestamp, Prior Team status, protection at signing, and transaction logs.
* **Counterexample**: Assuming cap room usage permanently blocks acquiring subsequent TPEs via separate concurrent or future trades overbroadly interprets **Art. VII §6(m)** [1, 15].

*(Note: This proof does not certify historical contract executions, 2020 amendments, or future balances.)*
